Fig. 2:HumanoidPose overview. (a) Retargeted human motions and randomized
rendering provide synthetic robot pose supervision. (b) Pseudo-labels from unlabeled
online videos adapt the detector through self-training. (c) Frozen human-pretrained
features and kinematic queries drive a shared decoder for joint angles and root pose.
Camera motion and forward kinematics place predictions in world coordinates.
The pose decoder is trained solely on synthetic data.

Fig. 3:The training corpus. Human motion capture retargeted onto sixteen humanoids
spanning3.0×3.0\timesin height (0.600.60–1.781.78m) and1919–4343degrees of freedom, rendered
in Unreal Engine under randomized scene, illumination and viewpoint. One sample is shown
per robot, paired with the configuration used to render it.

Fig. 4:Pose recovery across real humanoid platforms.
Self-recorded RGB frames (top) and predicted 3D configurations (bottom) for G1, PM01 and N1.
The same HumanoidPose model recovers locomotion, arm movements, crouching and
supported poses across different robot structures and appearances.
